rounds.text: Indraprastha Medical Corporation Ltd carries a premium valuation with a price-to-book ratio of 4.46x [E2], which is higher than the sector benchmark of 3.03x [E7]. This premium is difficult to justify given that the company's yearly operating-margin trend is inconsistent over the last year [E32], its quarterly operating-margin trend is inconsistent over the last two quarters [E33], and its earnings profile is cyclical [E58]. Furthermore, borrowings have increased to Rs 37 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 33 Cr a year earlier [E39], while domestic institutions have aggressively divested their holdings, dropping from 6.71% in Sep 2023 to just 0.59% in Jun 2026 [E43]. This institutional exit aligns with weak market sentiment, as the stock has delivered a twelve-month price return of -19.2% [E52], sits below its 200-day moving average [E68], and has a poor relative-strength rating of 31 against the Nifty 500 [E51]. Conceded: [E6], [E9], and [E38] show that the company trades at a lower P/E of 16.29x compared to the sector benchmark of 32.53x, boasts strong returns with an ROE of 24.8%, and maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x.
